web_title: 6. 10-Year Financial Forensics, Cash Conversion & Capital Allocation
book_title: Chapter 6: The Ten-Year Ledger — Margins, Cash Conversion & ROIC
question: How have Arista's revenue, margins, working capital, stock-based compensation, cash conversion, and return on invested capital compounded from FY2016 through Q3 2026?

epigraph.quote: Profit is an opinion; cash is a fact.
epigraph.author: Alfred Rappaport (paraphrased)

web_blocks.title: 6.1 Ten-Year Income Statement & Cash Flow Forensics (FY2016–9M 2026)

web_blocks.html: From FY2016 through FY2025, Arista Networks grew annual revenue nearly eightfold from $1.13 billion to $9.01 billion [1][6]. That marks a 26.0% compound annual growth rate [1][6]. Growth then sped up 44.3% YoY to $9.40 billion ($9,402.3 million) in the first nine months of FY2026 [2]. Operating leverage remained powerful as GAAP operating income grew nearly sixteenfold from $243.5 million in FY2016 (21.5% margin) to $3,856.1 million in FY2025 (42.8% margin), and reached $4,178.2 million (44.4% margin; 44.9% in Q3 2026, 49.1% non-GAAP) in 9M 2026 [1][2][3]. However, Q3 2026 Form 10-Q figures temper the assumption of uninterrupted gross margin stability: 9M 2026 GAAP gross margin compressed 160 basis points YoY to 62.9% (vs. 64.5% in 9M 2025), driven by a 150 bps decline in Product gross margin on memory/silicon scarcity and tariff-related product cost inflation [2].

web_blocks.caption: Arista Networks: 10-Year Historical P&L, Margins & Cash Flow Forensics (FY2016–9M 2026)
web_blocks.takeaway: Revenue grew ~8x from FY2016 to FY2025 while GAAP operating margin doubled from 21.5% to 42.8% (44.4% in 9M 2026). Yet 9M 2026 GAAP gross margin fell 160 bps YoY to 62.9% on memory and silicon cost inflation. Meanwhile, CFO conversion eased to 104.8% on -$962.8M inventory builds, and Q3 Net Income included a $135.8M strategic investment gain.

web_blocks.html: The ten-year ledger and Q3 2026 Form 10-Q footnotes reveal four key forensic truths. First, gross margin has softened under AI hardware and component inflation: while GAAP gross margin held between 63.8% and 64.5% in eight of ten years through FY2025, 9M 2026 GAAP gross margin slipped 160 bps YoY to 62.9% (63.6% in Q3 vs. 64.6% in Q3 2025) as memory and silicon tightness pushed product costs higher [1][2][6]. Second, R&D and SG&A discipline still expanded operating margins to 44.4% in 9M 2026 (even as R&D rose 32.6% YoY to $1,178.8 million on new product introduction outlays) [2]. Third, earnings quality in Q3 2026 benefited from non-operating gains: Other Income jumped to $273.1 million in Q3 2026 because it included $135.8 million of one-time gains on strategic investments (~7.1% of Q3 pre-tax profit) alongside $137.3 million of recurring Treasury interest [2]. Fourth, stock-based compensation (SBC) is growing in absolute dollars: 9M 2026 SBC rose +24.0% YoY to $379.4 million (4.0% of revenue; $138.1 million in Q3), and Note 5 discloses $1.7 billion of unamortized RSU compensation across 24.3 million unvested RSUs over a 4.1-year weighted-average period [2]. With share repurchases paused at $0 in 9M 2026, basic shares expanded by 6.9 million to 1,263.4 million (1,278.2 million diluted in Q3) [2].

web_blocks.title: 6.2 Balance Sheet Fortress, Working Capital & ROIC

web_blocks.html: Arista carries zero financial debt, with Debt/Equity and LT Debt/Equity both at 0.00 [1]. At year-end 2025, cash ($1,963.9 million) and marketable securities ($8,779.1 million) totaled $10,743.0 million [1]. By September 30, 2026, that reserve grew to $14,359.0 million, split between $2,288.1 million in cash and $12,070.9 million in marketable securities [2]. Note 2 shows the fixed-income portfolio carries a short 1.3-year weighted-average duration, though rising yields left $(117.2) million of gross unrealized losses in AOCI at September 30, 2026 [2]. Liquidity remains ample, with a Current Ratio of 3.29 and a Quick Ratio of 2.82 [2].

Working capital shifts explain both the 2022 cash dip, the 2024–2025 cash surge, and the 9M 2026 moderation. In FY2022, buffer inventory builds cut CFO-to-Net-Income conversion to 36.5% ($492.8 million CFO on $1,350.0 million net income) [6]. Once supply chains cleared, conversion rebounded to 130.2% in FY2024 and 124.5% in FY2025 [1][6]. In 9M 2026, however, CFO-to-Net-Income conversion moderated to 104.8% ($3,977.4 million CFO on $3,796.2 million net income, vs. 121.7% in 9M 2025) as inventories absorbed -$962.8 million in cash and accounts receivable absorbed -$440.9 million [2]. Crucially, Note 3 discloses that within $3,209.8 million of Q3 2026 inventory, raw materials surged +86.2% to $1,137.9 million and evaluation inventory at customer sites more than doubled (+116.6%) from $403.7 million to $874.3 million (27.2% of total inventory), while deferred COGS climbed 32.5% to $1,586.2 million [2]. Meanwhile, 9M 2026 CapEx more than doubled YoY to $184.9 million (vs. $82.5 million in 9M 2025), yielding $3,792.5 million in Free Cash Flow—a 40.3% FCF margin versus 47.2% in FY2025 [2].

web_blocks.takeaway: With 28.89% ROIC, zero debt, and $14.36B in cash and securities, Arista stays financially elite. Still, 9M 2026 footnotes flag 104.8% cash conversion, $874.3M in customer evaluation inventory, a $1.7B SBC overhang, and $0 buybacks.

web_blocks.html: Capital return has shifted from aggressive share reduction to cash retention during the AI supply buildout. Arista pays no cash dividend [1]. In FY2025, it spent $1.6 billion on open-market repurchases—3.6x its $439.2 million SBC expense—shrinking net share count [1]. In 9M 2026, management paused buybacks completely ($0 repurchased, leaving $817.9 million authorized). Equity-plan vesting lifted basic shares by 6.9 million to 1,263.4 million against $1.7 billion in unvested RSUs [2]. Even with $14.36 billion in cash, Arista earns 28.89% ROIC and 33.52% ROE. Those returns show elite compounding tempered by rising working-capital needs.

book_paragraphs: Numbers over ten years strip away all storytelling. Look at Arista's ten-year ledger from 2016 through 2025, and you see one of the cleanest financial compounding records in modern technology hardware.

In 2016, Arista generated 1.13 billion dollars in revenue and 243.5 million dollars in GAAP operating profit—a 21.5 percent operating margin. By 2025, revenue had grown nearly eightfold to 9.01 billion dollars, a 26 percent compound annual growth rate, while GAAP operating profit expanded nearly sixteenfold to 3.86 billion dollars, doubling the operating margin to 42.8 percent. In the first nine months of 2026 alone, revenue reached 9.40 billion dollars, already surpassing all of 2025.

Yet a rigorous audit of the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q reveals subtle shifts beneath those headline numbers. Outside the 2022–2023 semiconductor crunch, Arista held GAAP gross margins between 63.8 and 64.5 percent for eight of ten years—but in the first nine months of 2026, GAAP gross margin compressed 160 basis points year-over-year to 62.9 percent as memory and silicon scarcity lifted product costs. At the same time, cash flow from operations conversion moderated from 124.5 percent of net income in 2025 to 104.8 percent in 9M 2026 ($3.98 billion CFO, $3.79 billion FCF) because inventories absorbed 962.8 million dollars and CapEx more than doubled to 184.9 million dollars.

book_subsections.title: Cash Conversion, Stock-Based Compensation, and Zero Debt
paragraphs: In tech investing, you always have to check whether accounting profits turn into real cash or vanish into stock-based compensation, non-operating gains, and working capital. In 2025, Arista's stock-based compensation was 439.2 million dollars—just 4.9 percent of revenue—and buybacks of 1.6 billion dollars wiped out dilution more than three times over. In the first nine months of 2026, however, SBC grew 24 percent year-over-year to 379.4 million dollars with 1.7 billion dollars in unamortized RSU costs still ahead over the next four years. Because Arista paused share repurchases at zero dollars in 9M 2026, basic share count crept up by 6.9 million shares, while third-quarter GAAP net income also got a 135.8 million dollar lift from a one-time gain on strategic investments.

Working capital swings also require close attention. In 2022, stockpiling scarce components temporarily cut operating cash flow conversion to 36.5 percent of net income, before cash conversion snapped back to 124.5 percent in 2025. In 9M 2026, operating cash flow conversion moderated to 104.8 percent ($3.98 billion CFO on $3.80 billion net income) as evaluation inventory at customer sites more than doubled to 874.3 million dollars and raw materials surged 86 percent to 1.14 billion dollars—demonstrating that even an elite compounder absorbs meaningful cash when building ahead of an 800G/1.6T AI ramp.

On the balance sheet, Arista carries zero debt and held 14.36 billion dollars in cash and marketable securities at the end of September 2026. Even with that massive cash cushion sitting on the books, its Return on Invested Capital stands at 28.89 percent—nearly three times any reasonable cost of capital.

callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
callouts.text: When you and I finish a price-blind audit of Arista Networks, the verdict on business quality is unambiguous. It combines software-level margins and 28.89 percent ROIC with an eighteen-year owner-oriented CEO and a debt-free 14.36-billion-dollar balance sheet. The only reasons to stay vigilant are structural: 42 percent customer concentration in Microsoft and Meta, NVIDIA's bundled Spectrum-X push, and 11.4 billion dollars in binding purchase commitments.

book_subsections.title: Ten-Year Forensic Proof: Quality of Earnings and Capital Efficiency
paragraphs: Across a full ten-year arc from FY2016 through Q3 2026, Arista's financial statements read like a textbook case of high-ROIC compounding. Revenue expanded nearly eightfold from $1.13 billion in FY2016 to $9.01 billion in FY2025 before accelerating 44.3% in the first nine months of 2026. Over that same decade, GAAP operating margins more than doubled from 21.5% to 42.8% (reaching 44.9% in Q3 2026) because R&D and sales expenses scaled far more slowly than revenue.

More importantly, those accounting profits are backed by real cash. In FY2025, cash flow from operations reached $4.37 billion—124.5% of GAAP net income—and free cash flow hit $4.25 billion, a 47.2% free cash flow margin. Stock-based compensation stayed disciplined at 4.9% of revenue ($439.2 million), well below typical Silicon Valley software peers, allowing share buybacks to more than offset dilution. With $14.36 billion in cash and marketable securities and zero debt on the balance sheet, Arista enters any potential industry downturn from a position of extraordinary financial strength.

book_subsections.title: How Zero Debt and Disciplined Buybacks Compound Per-Share Value
paragraphs: Many high-growth technology companies flatter their non-GAAP profits by handing out massive stock-based compensation—often 15% to 25% of revenue—which quietly dilutes shareholders unless the company burns cash buying back shares. Arista stands apart. In FY2025, stock-based compensation totaled $439.2 million, or just 4.9% of revenue, while free cash flow reached $4.25 billion.

Because Arista carries zero long-term debt and earns interest on $14.36 billion of cash and marketable securities, every dollar of free cash flow belongs to equity owners. Management uses opportunistic share repurchases to shrink the share count over time and keeps plenty of liquidity on hand to fund supply-chain commitments during 58% growth surges without ever tapping debt markets.

book_subsections.title: Balance Sheet Fortress: Why $14.36 Billion in Net Cash Matters
paragraphs: In a cyclical technology downturn, debt turns a temporary revenue pause into an existential crisis. Arista carries zero short-term or long-term debt against $14.36 billion in cash and marketable securities as of September 30, 2026. That fortress balance sheet does three things for owners: it earns hundreds of millions in annual interest income at 4% to 5% Treasury yields, it lets Arista guarantee supply-chain commitments to win massive hyperscaler contracts, and it gives management dry powder to repurchase shares whenever market corrections create bargains.

book_subsections.title: Why Cash Flow Quality Beats Headline EPS
paragraphs: Headline earnings per share can always be massaged by aggressive revenue recognition or capitalized expenses, which is why serious owners check cash conversion first. Across FY2021 through FY2025, Arista's cumulative operating cash flow consistently matched or exceeded GAAP net income, culminating in 124.5% conversion in FY2025. When cash in the bank grows faster than reported accounting profit, earnings quality is high.
